描述_ZN: The Western Mount Huashan Temple Stele, Si Ming Ben, is one of the four types of topos of the Huashan stele that have been handed down to us, as it was hidden in Ningbo Fengxi Wanxian Shu Lou in the Ming Dynasty, and Ningbo was known as Si Ming in ancient times, so it was named after the place.　　The whole paper is mounted on a single shaft without cutting, preserving the original shape of the Han tablet and leaving the Tang inscriptions on both sides of the tablet, which are missing in the other three topographies. The inscriptions were made by Li Shangqing, Zhang Siqing, Cui Zhibai, Li Deyu, Cui Cui, Wang Shi and other famous ministers during the Dahe period (829-830) of the Tang Dynasty, as well as by Wang Ziwen in the eighth year of the Yuanfeng era (1085) of the Northern Song Dynasty. The entire painting measures 175 cm in length and 84.8 cm in width. The ancient paper is mottled and the ink color varies in intensity. Yan Kejun inscribed: "Like light clouds enveloping the moon, the gods and bones are all present", which is a superbly good phrase.　　Qianlong 52 years (1787), historian Qian Daxin for the compilation of the "Tianyi Pavilion Tablet" to visit Ningbo, Tianyi Pavilion master to four Ming this gift to Qian Daxin's son Dongbi, so this topography from Jiangnan to Beijing. At the end of the Qing Dynasty, this topography was given to Tuan Fang, the governor of the two rivers, whose daughter married Yuan Shikai's son, and used it as a dowry. In 1975, Hu offered it to the National Palace Museum.　　Song Ouyang Xiu "collection of ancient records", Hong Shi "official interpretation", Qing Ruan Yuan "Han Yanxi Xiyue Huashan Temple stele examination", Zhang Yansheng "good book of monuments and posters" and other books recorded.
